Function guide

Alpha

ALPHAFN evaluates an expression in a modified filter context. It is the most important function of the fixture language and it is used in almost every non-trivial measure written by practitioners, which is why the guide opens with it and returns to it repeatedly in later sections.

Beta

BETAFN returns a blank value when the denominator is zero. The first edition of the guide describes this behaviour briefly and refers readers to the reference page for the alternate-result argument, which most practitioners never use in practice but which exists for completeness.

Gamma

GAMMAFN requires a calendar table marked as a date table. Without the mark, the fixture language silently falls back to row-by-row evaluation, which produces totals that look plausible but are wrong across period boundaries; the guide therefore lists the mark as a precondition.

Delta

DELTAFN aggregates values over a table expression. It accepts any table, including one produced by another function, and it is the building block that the fixture language uses for every explicit iteration; practitioners meet it as soon as they leave simple sums behind.
